questions.subject: ACCOUNTING
questions.stem: Case 4301: Upland Company had beginning inventory of $5,850, net purchases of $3,800, and ending inventory of $300. What is cost of goods sold?

options.misconception: adds ending inventory instead of subtracting it
omits net purchases from the goods available for sale
reports ending inventory as the cost of goods sold

questions.explanation: Goods available for sale equal beginning inventory of $5,850 plus net purchases of $3,800. Subtracting the $300 still on hand at period end leaves $9,350 as the cost of goods sold. Adding ending inventory would double count goods that were never sold.
questions.hint: Beginning inventory plus purchases minus ending inventory gives the cost transferred out.
